# ligo_platform (Resource)

A a platform: a kind of system that targets live on, served by a plugin, with the identity provider and the secret store that it uses. A person decides every change to it, whatever the charter says: the provider files the change request once and waits for it (approval_timeout in the provider), and never approves one. It is never managed (there is no lock). Its config names a credential by reference, never by value.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A PostgreSQL platform that wires an identity provider and a secret store. A
# person decides every change to an instance, so each apply step waits for an
# approver (approval_timeout in the provider): the references make Terraform
# create the two instances first, and retire the platform before them.
resource "ligo_platform" "ledger" {
  name         = "pg-ledger"
  jurisdiction = "dc/corp-prod"
  realm        = "prod"
  type         = "postgres.v1"

  allowed_source_trust_domains = ["prod.example.org"]
  target_jurisdictions         = ["dc/corp-prod/*"]
  principal_prefix             = "svc_"

  identity_provider = {
    type     = ligo_identity_provider.directory.type
    instance = ligo_identity_provider.directory.name
  }
  secret_store = {
    type                    = ligo_secret_store.vault.type
    instance                = ligo_secret_store.vault.name
    secret_storage_strategy = "vault-static"
  }

  svid_selector = {
    match_expr        = "path == \"/ligo/plugin/postgres\""
    jwt_audience      = ["https://vault.example.org"]
    allow_shared_svid = true
  }

  # The bootstrap credential is a reference to a path in a store, never a value.
  config = jsonencode({
    host              = "pg.example.org"
    port              = 5432
    database          = "ledger"
    allowed_endpoints = ["pg.example.org:5432"]
    bootstrap_credential = {
      source       = "vault"
      address      = "https://vault.example.org:8200"
      auth_mount   = "jwt-spiffe"
      role         = "ligo-plugin-postgres"
      jwt_audience = "https://vault.example.org"
      kv_path      = "kv/data/ligo/bootstrap/postgres"
    }
  })
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `identity_provider` (Attributes) The identity provider instance it uses; ligo checks at the approval that it is ACTIVE and in the same realm. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--identity_provider))
- `jurisdiction` (String) The jurisdiction that owns it; a person on it decides every change. It cannot change.
- `name` (String) The name, unique among the instances of the kind; a new name is a new resource.
- `realm` (String) The realm; it cannot change.
- `secret_store` (Attributes) The secret store instance it uses; ligo checks at the approval that it is ACTIVE and in the same realm. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--secret_store))
- `type` (String) The plugin type and version, as server.yaml names it (such as vault.v1); it cannot change.

### Optional

- `allowed_source_trust_domains` (List of String) The trust domains of the sources that may use the platform.
- `check_existence` (Boolean) Whether the platform checks that a target exists before it is bound. Default: true.
- `config` (String, Sensitive) The plugin's configuration, as JSON text (jsonencode); some plugins (svid, none) have none. ligo checks it against the plugin's schema when the change is filed. It names a bootstrap credential by reference (a store, a path), never by value.
- `contacts` (Attributes List) Who to ask. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--contacts))
- `description` (String) What it is.
- `display_name` (String) A name for people.
- `namespace_template` (String) How the platform names what it creates for an account and a tenancy, such as {account}_{tenancy}.
- `network_flows` (String) The network flows the instance needs, as JSON text.
- `principal_prefix` (String) A prefix of the principals the platform creates, such as svc_.
- `rotation_interval` (String) How often the platform rotates credentials, such as 24h.
- `svid_selector` (Attributes) Which SVID is the plugin's, which the plugin process of the type has to present. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--svid_selector))
- `target_jurisdictions` (List of String) The jurisdiction patterns its targets may have. Default: its own jurisdiction and everything under it.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The name.
- `last_change_request` (String) The ID of the last change request the provider filed or waited for.
- `revision` (Number) The revision; an update names it, and ligo refuses a stale one.

### Nested Schema for `identity_provider`

Required:

- `instance` (String) Its name.
- `type` (String) Its plugin type.


<a id="nestedatt--secret_store"></a>
### Nested Schema for `secret_store`

Required:

- `instance` (String) Its name.
- `type` (String) Its plugin type.

Optional:

- `secret_storage_strategy` (String) How the platform keeps the credentials in the store; ligo defaults it when the store declares one.


<a id="nestedatt--contacts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `contacts`

Required:

- `name` (String) A name or a team.

Optional:

- `email` (String) Their address.


<a id="nestedatt--svid_selector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `svid_selector`

Required:

- `match_expr` (String) The expression that selects the SVID.

Optional:

- `allow_shared_svid` (Boolean) Whether other instances of the type may share the SVID.
- `jwt_audience` (List of String) The audiences of the JWT-SVID it sends to the bootstrap credential's store.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By name. A caller who may not file on its jurisdiction sees no config: the
# first plan then shows what the configuration sets.
terraform import ligo_platform.ledger pg-ledger
```
